title: orderfile: trace a compiled app's workloads, and accept symbol hints
body:
**What.** The linker order file is generated from a handful of sub-second runs, so it packs what a script's first
second touches. A large compiled TUI/CLI application that stays up enters ~13 MB of bun's code that those runs
never reach (DFG/FTL, the HTTP client, the standalone module graph, terminal text measurement, the idle
collector), scattered across .text: such an application keeps ~35 MB of .text resident at its idle prompt.

This adds (1) app-shaped workloads to `scripts/orderfile/generate.ts`: a ~500-module app compiled with
`bun build --compile --bytecode --splitting`, run one small feature per process on a pty in a fixed order;
(2) `--hints=<file>`: symbol lists placed first, matched across builds by normalised name; (3) `hints.ts`,
which writes such a list by tracing a real session of an application built on bun; (4) the tracer change
both need: following a compiled executable into re-executed copies of itself, one record per process.

| resident .text at the application's prompt (linux x64, 64 KB fault-around) | |
|---|---|
| today's order file | 34.9 MB measured |
| an earlier, smaller synthetic workload set | ≈23 MB measured |
| this suite | ≈20 MB modelled |
| the application's own hint list via `--hints` | 15.0 MB measured (12.2 modelled) |

`bun -e` is unchanged (3.0 MB modelled; it is still traced first). With `--hints` it costs ~1.8 MB more,
which is why hints are opt-in.

**How it was verified.** No relink: residency is modelled from the link map (section sizes + fault-around), the
model having matched the measured relinks above to within ~1 MB. generate.ts runs end to end against an existing
release build in 27–40 s (was 2m16 before the runs were pooled; CI step timeout is 15 min). Tests in
`test/js/bun/perf/linker-order.test.ts`.

**Limitations.** Linux/macOS only (the app's pty, unix-socket and shell features do not apply on Windows, and the
Windows tracer does not follow children). macOS is untested here: CI's trace-order step is soft-fail, a failing
feature is a warning, >10% failing is an error. On macOS the loader drops injected libraries through protected
binaries, so children mode is best-effort there. The feature order in features.txt was chosen by scoring
candidate orders against a function-entry trace of one such application; other applications will benefit
less. Numbers are modelled, not measured, for this exact suite.
